---
title: "Using smallvis"
description: "Install smallvis, make an embedding, plot it, and inspect the result."
---

`smallvis` lets you experiment with neighborhood embedding methods, including t-SNE and the LargeVis
and UMAP cost functions. You can change the input scaling, affinities, initialization, and optimizer
independently. Most methods use quadratic time and memory and suit small datasets;
[Barnes-Hut t-SNE](barnes-hut.html) provides an approximate route for larger inputs.

## Install

The package lives in the `smallvis` subdirectory of the repository. Install it and its dependencies,
including the GitHub plotting package [vizier](https://github.com/jlmelville/vizier), with:

```r
install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("jlmelville/smallvis/smallvis")
```

Installation from source requires an R-compatible C++ toolchain, such as Rtools on Windows.

## Make an embedding

`smallvis()` selects the numeric columns of a data frame, so the species column in `iris` stays out
of the calculation. Here t-SNE starts from scaled PCA coordinates and returns a two-column matrix.
Plotting during optimization is disabled so that the example also works in scripts.

```{r embedding}
library(smallvis)

embedding <- smallvis(
  iris,
  Y_init = "spca",
  perplexity = 30,
  epoch_callback = FALSE,
  n_threads = 1,
  verbose = FALSE
)
dim(embedding)
```

```{r plot, fig.alt="Two-dimensional t-SNE embedding of iris, with species distinguished by color and plotting symbol."}
species <- as.integer(iris$Species)
plot(
  embedding,
  col = c("#0072B2", "#D55E00", "#009E73")[species],
  pch = species,
  xlab = "t-SNE 1",
  ylab = "t-SNE 2"
)
```

The coordinates describe a neighborhood embedding: nearby points are the relationships the method
tries to preserve. The [perplexity experiments](perplexity.html) show how changing the neighborhood
size changes the picture.

## Inspect the result

Set `ret_extra = TRUE` to return a list containing the coordinates in `Y`, final objective
contributions in `costs`, and an optimization history in `itercosts`.

```{r result}
fit <- smallvis(
  iris,
  Y_init = "spca",
  perplexity = 30,
  ret_extra = TRUE,
  epoch_callback = FALSE,
  n_threads = 1,
  verbose = FALSE
)
c(iterations = fit$iter, final_cost = sum(fit$costs))
```

The final cost is evaluated at the returned coordinates after removing exaggeration. Values in the
history were recorded during optimization and can include exaggeration. The
[function reference](../reference/smallvis.html#value) describes the available diagnostics, including
optional matrices that can be expensive to calculate or retain.

## Plot during optimization

The default `epoch_callback = TRUE` uses `vizier` to plot progress. You can also supply your own
callback. This example colors points by species and puts the iteration number in the title:

```{r callback, eval=FALSE}
iris_plot <- function(Y, iter, cost = NULL) {
  plot(Y, col = as.integer(iris$Species), main = paste("Iteration", iter))
}
smallvis(iris, Y_init = "spca", epoch_callback = iris_plot)
```
